title: KEY-SUBANCHOR-SCALE: is sub-anchor structure dead for taxonomy reasons or data reasons? (zero calls, KEY only)

criteria.text: PRIMARY: (model, anchor)-demeaned cross-tree r on the most-changed third of questions at full size vs its within-anchor null 95th
criteria.value: literal statistic r = +0.0828 (n 3,735) vs null 95th +0.0237 (0 of 200 above): the falsifier's literal condition; checker: 1,378 of the 3,735 (37%) are NESTED pairs (the bareq leaf entirely inside the abt2d leaf; 1,189 exactly nested; shared cell-mates 59.4 vs 24.7 under the null; the within-anchor null produces 0 nested pairs), so the instrument is invalid across trees of different granularity; on questions whose cell genuinely changes: containment < 0.5 (n 1,910) +0.0059 (75 of 200 null reps above); < 0.25 (n 1,239) -0.0665 (below all 200): the substantive reading REFUTED; the prediction HOLDS on genuinely changed cells
criteria.denominator: 3,735 most-changed-third questions; 134,460 pairs; null 200 reps; ARENA12 key

criteria.text: the trend of that r with cell size
criteria.value: 25% (52 q/cell) +0.0607 [2 of 5 draws negative] vs null 95th +0.0296; 50% (92) +0.0691 vs +0.0281; 100% (184) +0.0828 vs +0.0237; slope +0.0122 per doubling; total movement 0.022 across 4x, inside the null's spread (up to 0.040); the trended quantity inherits the nesting artefact

criteria.text: whether 900-1,500 q/leaf is on the trend line
criteria.value: NO: log-linear r(900) +0.1103, r(1,500) +0.1193; SB from the full-size point +0.3066 / +0.4243; 0.70 needs ~3e17 q/leaf; the within-tree split-half reliability of the demeaned key sub-anchor profile is already 0.73 (bareq) / 0.75 (abt2d) while cross-tree r on cross-cutting questions is null or negative: no cell size brings it to 0.70

predictions.text: still negative or null on the most-changed third at full size, for both trees: sub-anchor structure is not tree-stable even on the training questions (closed for TAXONOMY reasons)
predictions.value: builder scored FAILED; checker's number wins: on every stratum of genuinely changed cells (containment < 0.5 +0.006 inside the null; < 0.25 -0.067 below it) the statistic is null or negative for both anchor conventions; the prediction is not shown to fail

falsifier.text: a positive, null-clearing r on the most-changed third at full size reopens sub-anchor as a data question
falsifier.note: its literal condition is met by the Jaccard-tercile statistic, but the tercile is an invalid 'most-changed' instrument across trees of different granularity and the within-anchor null does not preserve what the stratum conditions on (both standing rules); the substantive claim is not established; sub-anchor stays closed for taxonomy reasons; the Jaccard tercile must be replaced by a containment stratum before this line is reopened

plain_description.what: Compares two trees of different granularity on about 11,200 answer-key questions. On questions whose cell changes most between the trees, it asks whether model strengths below the topic level agree across trees. It also checks how this changes with cell size. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: Asks whether structure below the topic level failed because the taxonomy is not real or only because cells had too few questions.
plain_description.information: Agreement that grows with more data would reopen the sub-topic line as a data problem. Null or negative agreement would close it as a taxonomy problem. Result: the registered statistic was positive, but a checker showed this came from nested cells, which agree by construction. On questions whose cell really changes, agreement is null or negative. The prediction is not shown to fail, but the sub-topic line stays closed for taxonomy reasons on this evidence. The measure must be redone before the line is reopened.
